clue.text: Alaric got his cooked after six

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the Roman numeral

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: cooked means these letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of someone's dinner prepared after six o'clock, with a Gothic king's name attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges GOT HIS into SIGOTH, which follows VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaric was the king of the western Goths who sacked Rome in 410, so he is an example of that people.

clue.text: The peri of the Savoy

parts.note: the fairy heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera subtitled The Peer and the Peri, first staged at the Savoy Theatre

explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy of Persian legend; the Savoy operas are Gilbert and Sullivan's.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy title character of the 1882 Gilbert and Sullivan Savoy opera.

clue.text: Untimely warmth displayed by a Calcutta mathematician ?

parts.note: Calcutta is in India, so a person from there is Indian
one who does sums, a summer

explanation.surface: Unseasonable heat blamed on a mathematician from Calcutta.
explanation.walkthrough: A summer is read as 'one who sums', a joke on the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of warm weather in autumn, after summer should be over, is warmth out of season.

clue.text: Civil Defence notice redesigned for the West

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: CD stands for Civil Defence

explanation.surface: A Civil Defence poster revamped for Western use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges CD and NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the western world, as opposed to the Orient.

clue.text: Little John German orders cabs

parts.note: Hans is the German pet form of Johannes, John
OM is the Order of Merit, so OMS are orders

explanation.surface: A small German named John places orders for taxis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' marks a short, familiar form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-wheeled horse-drawn carriages for hire, the taxis of Victorian London.

clue.text: Piano in inset perhaps ? More like a harpsichord

indicators.note: in puts the piano's letter inside the rearranged word
perhaps suggests the word inset could be otherwise arranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Is a piano in an inset picture really closer to a harpsichord?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges INSET to SINET; 'in' places P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small keyboard instrument with plucked strings, a compact relative of the harpsichord.

clue.text: Some conflagration in Uttar Pradesh

definitions.note: the city, home of the Taj Mahal, located in that northern Indian state

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A fire breaking out in a northern Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found in Uttar Pradesh, the state in northern India.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Yamuna famous for the Taj Mahal lies within that Indian state.

clue.text: He learns his languages parrot-fashion, do we hear ?

definitions.text: He learns his languages parrot-fashion, do we hear

parts.words: He learns his languages parrot-fashion, do we hear
parts.note: a speaker of many tongues, whose name sounds like a parrot, Polly, plus a word for speech

explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the stock name for a parrot; 'do we hear' points to the sound of the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fluent in many tongues; the Greek roots mean many and tongue.

clue.text: A spread once noted in Tara's halls ?

definitions.text: A spread once noted in Tara's halls

parts.words: A spread once noted in Tara's halls
parts.note: Thomas Moore's song begins 'The harp that once through Tara's halls'; a chord spread out note by note is played in the harp's manner

explanation.surface: A recollection of a feast laid out long ago at the ancient seat of Irish kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests food, but it is a chord spread out; the Italian word comes from arpa, harp, the instrument of Moore's song about Tara.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord whose notes sound one after another, as on a harp, which is the musical term the clue describes.

clue.text: Malodorous and lacking a cover

parts.note: lacking suggests nothing at all, the letter O as zero
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Something smelly with its top left off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'lacking a cover' as nought plus a lid; the word is a rare one meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare dictionary adjective for having a strong, offensive smell.

clue.text: Maybe Darcy is noisy, it's just his way

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark excusing Mr Darcy's loudness as simply part of his character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges all of DARCY IS NOISY.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal quirk or peculiar habit of behaviour is a particular person's own way.

clue.text: Salmon's colourful American relation

parts.note: a fish of the salmon family, native to North America, with iridescent stripes

explanation.walkthrough: Salmon looks like a surname or colour; it is the fish, and colourful hints at the rainbow stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American game fish of the salmon family with a pink lateral band.

clue.text: Club-man's position

parts.note: reads like a member's status in a gentlemen's club, but means how a golfer holding a club sets his feet

explanation.walkthrough: A clubman suggests a social club; here it is a golfer with his club, addressing the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The way a player stands with feet placed before striking the ball is his posture at address.

clue.text: Concerning the measurement of feet ?

parts.note: sounds like shoe sizing, but the feet are units of verse rhythm, and also a nod to the system of measures

explanation.walkthrough: Feet here are poetic feet, the units of verse rhythm, not body parts or imperial lengths.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for verse composed in regular rhythm, relating to its scansion and measure.

clue.text: Repay again completely

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
quite means completely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: An instruction to settle a debt a second time, in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a kindness or avenge a wrong is to make a return for it.

clue.text: Excessive greed is a blow to a business centre

parts.note: a rap is a blow, a sharp knock
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A comment that greed does damage to a commercial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping, predatory desire for money or possessions is extreme avarice.

clue.text: Tall talk, to brag about the doctor

indicators.note: about means the boasting goes around the doctor's letters

parts.note: to boast is to brag
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A boastful person bragging about their physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MB inside BOAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall talk is pompous, inflated speech, which is exactly what grandiloquent empty rhetoric is.

clue.text: But it's regular working hours for cricketers

definitions.text: But it's regular working hours for cricketers

parts.words: But it's regular working hours for cricketers
parts.note: extra hours at work, but cricketers spend all their playing time bowling sets of six balls

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, so play is all over-time.
explanation.definitionFit: Time worked beyond the normal hours, punningly the normal time of cricketers.

clue.text: Flight of ratings in disorderly speed

definitions.text: Flight of ratings in disorderly speed

parts.words: Flight of ratings in disorderly speed
parts.note: sailors fleeing in a disorderly rush; the scramble of the word speed hints at the ending

explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors; a flight here is a fleeing, not an air trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a crowd or herd in one direction.

clue.text: Urge Tom to become an epicure

indicators.note: to become means the letters turn into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Encouraging a man called Tom to take up fine dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges URGE TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of good food and drink is a person of refined taste at table.

clue.text: Plant helps in manufacture of pencils

definitions.meaning: a flowering shrub, leadwort, with blue flowers
another name for graphite, the pencil 'lead'

explanation.surface: A factory where some greenery assists in making pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the leadwort shrub and graphite, the black carbon used for pencil cores.

clue.text: Cockney's port is a shady retreat

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls his harbour a pleasant shady place.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy bower formed by trees or climbing plants trained over a frame.

clue.text: Swathe in continental shawl

parts.note: en is French for in
a wrap is a shawl

explanation.surface: Someone bundled up in a shawl bought on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe something is to wind cloth around it, to envelop it.

clue.text: Pooh-Bah as supplier of narrative detail, for instance :

definitions.text: Pooh-Bah as supplier of narrative detail, for instance

parts.words: Pooh-Bah as supplier of narrative detail, for instance
parts.note: in The Mikado Pooh-Bah calls his invented details 'merely corroborative detail, intended to give artistic verisimilitude to an otherwise bald and unconvincing narrative'

explanation.walkthrough: Pooh-Bah is the pompous holder of every office in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, famous for that line.
explanation.definitionFit: One who supplies confirming evidence that backs up a story, as Pooh-Bah claims to do.

clue.text: Appropriate-sounding ceremony

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word pronounced the same as the synonym

parts.note: right means appropriate, fitting

explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns RIGHT into its soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal religious or solemn ritual observance.

clue.text: Uncle Sam's exclamation on seeing the moulding ?

parts.note: an American might exclaim 'Oh, gee!'; the first part is O
an American might exclaim 'Oh, gee!'; the first part is O

explanation.surface: An American's cry of wonder at some fancy plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam stands for an American; 'Oh gee' gives the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-shaped curve used in architectural mouldings and arches.

clue.text: Full name of the bird who tells tales

definitions.text: Full name of the bird who tells tales

parts.words: Full name of the bird who tells tales
parts.note: a tell-tale is a tit, as in tit for tat; the bird's longer, full name adds a small rodent

explanation.walkthrough: The common short name for the small songbird is tit; this is its full, older name.
explanation.definitionFit: The older full name of the small songbird usually called a tit.

clue.text: Herein scenes of warlike and other operations

definitions.text: Herein scenes of warlike and other operations

parts.words: Herein scenes of warlike and other operations
parts.note: places of war, operating rooms in hospitals and playhouses where scenes are acted all share one name

explanation.walkthrough: The plural covers theatres of war, operating theatres and stage theatres, where scenes are played.
explanation.definitionFit: Playhouses where scenes are staged, regions of military action, and rooms for surgery all share the name.
